At stake on college campuses today is the status of students as intellectuals—but to shift the discussion to this terrain requires a radical reimagining of who gets to be an intellectual in the first place.

The problem is that current academia is anti-intellectual. They have taken their practice of redefining words and concepts to achieve their political and social goals so far, they are now devoid of real meaning and no discussion of ideas is allowed. These "students" are neither students nor intellectuals. Their professors are if anything worse. The administrators are all either craven cowards or simply like the professoriate but with more power.

The goal of education, in other words, is not only to teach skills. Education prepares students to be intellectuals in the Gramscian sense—that is, to be in the condition to govern, and thus to reorganize, at the very least, the university they attend.

No actually, that is not the purpose. Indeed it is anathema to the purpose. Even accepting the argument that a university education is about more than job training, it does not follow students are or should be in any position to dictate the governance of the school. If school is where they learn logical thinking, argument, and the ability to govern, then the school needs to be organized to do so. Since the students have not yet been trained to govern allowing them power to change how the school operates, what it teaches, etc is completely opposite of the purpose.

This week, the Afrikan/Black Student Alliance at the University of California at Santa Cruz reclaimed Kerr Hall with a list of demands. The demands were reasonable, by nearly any measure: They would like to live together in guaranteed housing; they would like to have a designated social space inside that housing; they would like to choose colors of black liberation and diaspora for the exterior of the housing; and they would like “mandatory in-person diversity competency training.”

Calling those demands reasonable just shows how incredibly anti-intellectual universities have become. They no longer are places to learn new ideas or to challenge one's intellect. They are now simply places to learn a single outlook (though each group which doesn't identify with Western culture can learn their own special grievance culture) to be carried out into the world. This is not learning intellectualism and how to govern a complex society.
